1	# product-wiki — the self-growing product research wiki
2	
3	This project keeps its market/user/competitor research as a self-growing wiki
4	under `product-wiki/` (Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern: compile findings once, refine in
5	place). Layout, required page sections, the Key insights header's shape,
6	growth-log dating, source links, staleness, and the isolation wall are
7	**check-enforced** — the finding is the instruction, so this prose never restates
8	them. The full growth procedure is the pack's task doc
9	(`packs/product-wiki/tasks/wiki-growth/task.md`).
10	
11	- **Every page opens with what it found.** `## Key insights` leads the page: a
12	  few bullets carrying the research's actual conclusions — the numbers, the
13	  competitor that already does this, the thing that turned out not to be true —
14	  enough that a human who reads only the header understands what was researched
15	  and what it means. Not a table of contents ("covers pricing and competitors"),
16	  not a teaser. The body is where the reader goes for evidence, nuance and
17	  citations; the header is where they decide whether they need to.
18	- **Terse, plain, and only the non-obvious.** One short line per bullet, in
19	  ordinary words — no qualifying clause, no citation, no hedge, no jargon a
20	  newcomer would have to decode. Prefer the finding that would *surprise*
21	  someone who knows the field: the thing that turned out not to be true, the
22	  number nobody expects, the competitor who already shipped it. Whether a point
23	  is obvious is genuinely hard to call, so **don't agonise — when in doubt, keep
24	  it**. A borderline-obvious line costs the reader two seconds; a long, careful
25	  line costs them the header.
26	- **The header is a current view, not a log.** A pass that changes what a page's
27	  most important findings are rewrites the header to match — a superseded
28	  insight leaves it (the correction and its why stay in the body, per below),
29	  and an insight the pass didn't touch stays put. If nothing changed the page's
30	  top-line understanding, the header doesn't move.
31	- **The sink is human-reviewed only.** `product-wiki/product-requirements/` never
32	  changes as a side effect of wiki work or any unattended pass — a wiki finding
33	  that should move a requirement gets a growth-log note (and a repo issue) and
34	  waits for a human. It is the only `product-wiki/` content the rest of the repo may
35	  build on.
36	- **Compile once, refine in place.** Read the target page end to end before
37	  researching; `## Open questions` is the backlog — research what it flags as
38	  open, thin, or dated, and spot-check an existing citation or two per pass.
39	  Never re-derive a claim that's already cited and current.
40	- **Cited, never silently rewritten.** An uncited claim doesn't get written. A
41	  wrong or superseded claim is corrected with a note of why (and its source),
42	  never deleted without trace. Every real change records itself in the page's
43	  growth log and updates the open questions in both directions.
44	- **No fabricated growth.** Most passes find little or nothing; no new citable
45	  material → no edit, no log entry, no PR.
46	- **sample-data and new wikis.** `product-wiki/sample-data/` gains a file only when
47	  a wiki claim needs one to point to — never test fixtures (anything a test
48	  asserts against belongs in engineering's tree). Any folder under `product-wiki/`
49	  outside the two reserved names *is* a wiki (the structural classifier), so
50	  create one only deliberately, seeded with its required sections; automation
51	  refines existing pages, it never invents new ones.
52	- **Review discipline.** Unattended growth always lands as an unmerged PR —
53	  researched claims entering a committed knowledge base need the review gate.
54	  The owner phrase **"grow the product wiki"** runs the worker method
55	  in-session with full web tooling: same rules, same PR discipline.

1	# Business
2	
3	Business models and price anchors for Claudinite: what adjacent devtools
4	charge, which commercial archetypes survive contact with a "plain vendored
5	files, no server" product, and what is genuinely scarce enough to price.
6	Method lessons live in [`Methods/`](../Methods/README.md); who would pay in
7	[`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md). Nothing on this page is a decision —
8	the human-reviewed distillation is
9	[`product-requirements/`](../product-requirements/README.md).
10	
11	## Key insights
12	
13	- Vendored files are trivially copyable — the sellable scarcities are the convergence bot, canon updates, private packs, and SLA.
14	- Governance tooling prices at $19–29/seat/mo (Copilot Business, GitLab Premium); AI-multiplier tools reach $60–200.
15	- pre-commit.ci's $0-for-OSS / $10–100/mo flat org tiers is the closest live pricing precedent for a config-bot product.
16	- Only GitHub Apps can be paid Marketplace listings (95% to publisher) — Actions and plain files cannot.
17	- Spotify sells its paid Backstage plugins only via negotiated AWS private offers — self-serve paid content looked weak.
18	- Sponsorware is hobby-scale: GitHub Sponsors totals ~$100M cumulative over ~7 years across ~70k maintainers.
19	- Behavioral seats (Snyk: committed in 90 days; CodeRabbit: opened a PR) are the emerging norm for repo-attached tools.
20	
21	## Price anchors (mid-2026)
22	
23	Caveat on provenance: several vendor pricing pages 403-block fetchers; where
24	a price rests on vendor-domain search quotes rather than a directly-opened
25	page, the source bullet says so.
26	
27	**AI assistant/agent seats** (what the target user already pays):
28	
29	- GitHub Copilot: Free / Pro $10 / Pro+ $39 / Max $100 per user/mo
30	  (vendor page, opened directly); Business $19, Enterprise $39 per user/mo
31	  (GitHub docs).
32	- Cursor: Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200; team seats $32 (Standard) and $96
33	  (Premium) per seat/mo annual, after the June 2026 teams-pricing change
34	  (vendor pages via search quotes).
35	- Claude: Pro $20, Max $100–200; Team Standard $25/seat (5-seat min), Team
36	  Premium $100/seat annual — Claude Code rides Premium seats; Enterprise
37	  custom (triangulated secondary sources; vendor page blocked).
38	
39	**Repo-attached quality/governance tooling** (the band Claudinite would be
40	judged in):
41	
42	- Codecov Team $5 / Pro $12 per user/mo; Snyk Team $25 per contributing
43	  dev/mo (caps at 10 licenses before forced sales contact).
44	- CodeRabbit Lite $12 / Pro $24 / Pro Plus $48 per dev/mo annual — billing
45	  only devs who open PRs.
46	- SonarQube Cloud prices the *codebase*, not the humans: from $32/mo per
47	  100k LOC — the notable per-repo-style metric.
48	- pre-commit.ci: $0 open source, $10/mo personal private, $20/mo org ≤25
49	  users, $100/mo org ≤100 users (Marketplace listing, opened directly).
50	- Atlassian Compass was the scorecard category's floor at $0/$8/$25 per
51	  user/mo — now being sunset into DX (see Customers wiki for the
52	  consolidation signal).
53	- Enterprise scorecard platforms (transaction data, not list prices):
54	  OpsLevel ~$400–700/dev/yr; Cortex enterprise contracts $100k–250k+/yr;
55	  Port free ≤15 seats then quote-gated with SSO/RBAC/audit behind Enterprise.
56	- GitLab open-core: Free / Premium $29 / Ultimate ~$99 per user/mo, Duo AI
57	  add-on +$19 — the paid line drawn at org-level controls, not core function.
58	- npm private packages: $7/user/mo — the canonical private-registry price.
59	
60	## Archetypes that survive "plain files, no server"
61	
62	Each with its named precedent and the implication for Claudinite:
63	
64	- **Hosted-service-on-OSS** (pre-commit.ci, Renovate/Mend): the files and
65	  mechanism are free; the *bot that runs the loop for you* is the product.
66	  Claudinite's equivalent sellable: operating the nightly
67	  baselining/convergence fleet and the scheduled agentic maintenance. The
68	  strongest-fit archetype — it prices exactly what is ongoing.
69	- **Open-core / enterprise edition** (GitLab, Mend Renovate EE): core free,
70	  paid tier at org-level controls — scale, reporting, compliance, SLA. Maps
71	  to fleet reporting, private canon, multi-team controls.
72	- **Private-registry pattern** (npm, Docker Hub): public packs free, private
73	  packs paid (~$7–24/user/mo band). Maps directly to "your org's private
74	  canon and packs."
75	- **Support/SLA subscription** (Tidelift): validated as strategic value but
76	  acquired (Sonar, Dec 2024) rather than scaled standalone — treat as a
77	  deal-sweetener, not the model.
78	- **Paid content on a free platform** (Spotify's Backstage plugin bundle):
79	  exists, but Spotify retreated from public self-serve pricing to AWS
80	  Marketplace private offers — read as weak self-serve demand for paid
81	  plugins; enterprise-negotiated deals instead. A warning against "sell the
82	  packs themselves."
83	- **Marketplace billing** (GitHub): publishers keep 95%, but only GitHub
84	  *Apps* can be paid listings — Actions and files cannot. Marketplace
85	  distribution/billing would require wrapping Claudinite's loop in a GitHub
86	  App, which pushes toward the hosted-bot model anyway.
87	- **Sponsorware**: ceiling too low to matter commercially — ~$100M
88	  *cumulative* across ~70k maintainers in ~7 years; mid-tier maintainers
89	  $500–5k/mo.
90	
91	One-time content sales have no working precedent in this space at product
92	scale — though the indie segment does pay $199–249 one-time for
93	boilerplates (see [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md)), which suggests a
94	one-time *entry* SKU is viable even if recurring revenue must come from the
95	loop.
96	
97	## What the anchors suggest
98	
99	- Per-seat: $10–40/seat/mo is defensible for governance-positioned tooling
100	  (between Codecov's $5 and Copilot Enterprise's $39); the $60–200 AI-premium
101	  band applies only if positioned as a capability multiplier, not
102	  governance.
103	- Flat org tiers: pre-commit.ci's $20/mo (≤25 users) and $100/mo (≤100
104	  users) is the credible low-end floor; per-repo or per-LOC metrics
105	  (SonarQube-style) are the alternative if seats fit badly.
106	- Seat definition: behavioral ("developers whose repos consume a pack" /
107	  "opened a PR in a governed repo") mitigates the uneven-adoption objection,
108	  per Snyk and CodeRabbit precedent.
109	- The free tier is load-bearing in every surviving precedent: free for
110	  public/OSS repos is how pre-commit.ci, Renovate, Codecov and CodeRabbit
111	  all built their funnels.
112	
113	## Sources

116	- [Copilot org billing — GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/concepts/billing/organizations-and-enterprises) — Business/Enterprise seats
117	- [Cursor teams pricing change](https://cursor.com/blog/teams-pricing-june-2026) and [teams pricing docs](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/pricing) — via search quotes (site 403s fetchers)
118	- [Claude Team pricing 2026 — tygartmedia](https://tygartmedia.com/claude-team-pricing-2026-standard-premium-seats/), corroborated by [aipricing.guru](https://www.aipricing.guru/subscriptions/claude-team-premium/) and [intuitionlabs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/claude-pricing-plans-api-costs) — secondary triangulation

132	## Open questions
133	
134	- Direct confirmation of Cursor/Claude/Snyk/Codecov/Sonar prices on their own
135	  pricing pages (all 403'd this pass; figures rest on vendor-domain search

137	- Mend Renovate Enterprise's real price (contact-sales; the $250/dev/yr

151	
152	- **2026-07-31** — page created in the owner-directed ecosystem research
153	  pass: price anchors collected across AI-assistant seats, repo-attached

1	# Customers
2	
3	Customer profiles and potential users for Claudinite, in three segments:
4	independent developers, small software shops and agencies (2–50 devs), and
5	large enterprises (100+ engineers, platform teams). For each: who they are,
6	what they do today instead, the trigger moment, and what they would pay.
7	Price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); what this implies
8	for the offering in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).
9	
10	## Key insights
11	
12	- 90% of developers use AI at work; only ~24–33% trust its output — the adoption/trust scissor is the buying condition.
13	- Claude Code went from ~3% to 18% work usage in eight months with the category's best satisfaction — the fastest-growing agent.
14	- Users file issues literally titled "need enforcement mechanism"; org-wide shared CLAUDE.md is an open 40-👍 request.
15	- Solo devs run dotfiles and symlinks; agencies copy a shared config repo per client — drift machines with no update path.
16	- Indies pay $199–249 one-time for vendored starter files (ShipFast: $250k in 5 months); shops absorb $125/seat for Claude Premium.
17	- Enterprise near-blockers, in order: security review, multi-agent (AGENTS.md) support, private canon — then metrics and SLA.
18	- Spotify's Fleetshift proved the mechanism at scale: 270k+ fleet PRs, 77% automerged — enterprises already hold this mental model.
19	
20	## The market condition: adoption up, trust down
21	
22	- Stack Overflow 2025 (49k+ respondents): 84% use or plan to use AI tools
23	  (up from 76%), 51% of professionals use them daily — while favorable
24	  sentiment fell to 60% and 46% actively distrust output accuracy; 66% name
25	  "almost right, but not quite" solutions as their top frustration. Only 31%
26	  currently use *agents*; 87% of respondents are concerned about agent
27	  accuracy — Stack Overflow's own framing is "agents on a leash."
28	- DORA 2025 (≈5,000 respondents): 90% of developers use AI at work, 80%+
29	  report productivity gains, yet 30% report little or no trust in
30	  AI-generated code. Its central finding: AI *amplifies* existing
31	  organizational strengths and dysfunctions; quality internal platforms and
32	  a "clear and communicated AI stance" are named mediating capabilities —
33	  and AI adoption still correlates with delivery *instability* where control
34	  systems (testing, version control, feedback loops) haven't kept up.
35	- JetBrains (24,534 devs, 2025): 85% regularly use AI for coding but only
36	  44% call it integrated into their workflow; by its January 2026 pulse, 90%
37	  used at least one AI tool at work.
38	- Claude Code specifically: 18% work usage by January 2026 (24% US/Canada),
39	  up from ~3% mid-2025, with category-best satisfaction (CSAT 91, NPS 54);
40	  Anthropic announced $1B annualized run-rate within ~6 months of GA
41	  (Dec 2025). GitHub Copilot leads usage at 29% but has flatlined.
42	
43	The scissor — near-universal use, low trust, "almost right" output — is the
44	condition a machine-enforced-conventions product sells into: human vigilance
45	does not scale with agent output volume.

47	## Segment: independent developers
48	
49	- **Who**: ~14% of Stack Overflow respondents are freelancers; SlashData
50	  counts 47.2M developers worldwide (36.5M professional) — a ~5M freelance
51	  professional ceiling before filtering to agent users. r/ClaudeAI reached
52	  ~1M members by mid-2026 (+37% in one 90-day window).
53	- **What they do today**: version-control `~/.claude` in a dotfiles repo,
54	  symlink CLAUDE.md/commands/hooks across projects, with explicit gitignore
55	  allowlists; the pattern is common enough that dedicated tools exist
56	  (dot-claude-sync, claude-code-dotfiles). This solves one *machine's*
57	  consistency, not cross-repo drift.
58	- **Documented pain**: multiple anthropics/claude-code issues (verified via
59	  GitHub API 2026-07-31) — #18660 "CLAUDE.md instructions are read but not
60	  reliably followed — need enforcement mechanism", #34132 "Rules in
61	  .claude/rules/ and CLAUDE.md are advisory-only", #32193 "Claude violates
62	  its own mandatory CLAUDE.md instructions"; plus blog posts like "I wrote
63	  200 lines of rules for Claude Code. It ignored them all."
64	- **Trigger moment**: the Nth repo whose CLAUDE.md has drifted from the
65	  others, or the agent visibly violating rules it was given.
66	- **Willingness to pay**: already paying $10–200/mo for the agent itself;
67	  demonstrated $199–249 one-time for vendored starter files (Marc Lou's
68	  ShipFast: $250k in its first 5 months, "own it forever" as the pitch) and
69	  $5–27 for Gumroad rules packs. Realistic band: ~$10–19/mo, or a $29–79

71	- **What matters in Claudinite's shape**: plain files (matches how they
72	  already share conventions — the awesome-lists at 51k/40k stars are

101	## Segment: large enterprises (100+ engineers)
102	
103	- **Who buys**: platform-engineering/DevEx teams — Gartner: 80% of large
104	  software-engineering orgs will have platform teams by 2026 (up from 45% in
105	  2022); DORA: 90% of orgs have at least one internal platform. DX's survey
106	  of budget holders: 38% spent $101–500 per developer per year on AI dev
107	  tools in 2025; about half reserve 1–3% of engineering budget for AI
108	  tooling. Booking.com's DevEx team is the documented example of the buying
109	  center (procures AI tools, justifies with DX telemetry).
110	- **Scale of rollouts**: Uber ~90% of engineers on Cursor/Claude Code with
111	  in-house uReview gating; Accenture ~12,000 devs on Copilot; Infosys
112	  ~18,000; TELUS 57,000 employees on Claude; DX's Q4-2025 dataset (135k
113	  developers, 435 companies): 91% adoption, 22% of merged code AI-authored,
114	  and enterprises deploying "access controls, logging, approved model
115	  policies, and CI policy gates — not simply open access."
116	- **The precedent they hold**: Spotify's Fleet Management created 270,000+
117	  automated PRs across thousands of repos in 2022, 77% automerged — and its
118	  2025 Honk background agent (1,500+ merged AI PRs) rides the same
119	  infrastructure with CI/test gating and constraints on what the agent may
120	  touch. Puppet/Chef desired-state convergence is the older mental model:
121	  agents check in, compare to desired state, remediate drift. "Puppet for
122	  agent conventions, converging via reviewable PRs" is legible to any
123	  platform team.
124	- **Segmentation note**: the top ~20% (DORA "harmonious high-achievers" —
125	  the Ubers and Spotifys) build this in-house; the bottom ~10% lack

130	  proving appetite for exactly Claudinite's delivery shape at the

132	  unclaimed).
133	- **Ranked requirements a sale would face** (each grounded in the research;
134	  hardest first): (1) security/supply-chain review — SOC 2 or a compensating

139	  so Claude-Code-only addresses a slice of the fleet; (3) private canon in
140	  the customer's own tenancy; (4) central non-overridable enforcement with

3	The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
4	coding-agent user already has on disk, the platform-native layer Anthropic now
5	ships itself, the direct rule-sync competitors, the adjacent content
6	ecosystems, and the enterprise vendors encroaching from above. Business models
7	and price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); customer
8	segments in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md); what this means for
9	Claudinite in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).

11	## Key insights
12	
13	- Anthropic now ships the session half natively: plugins bundle skills+hooks+MCP and can be force-enabled org-wide.
14	- Nobody — native or rival — converges repos: no auto-PR loop from a canon, no CI convention gates, no shared growth loop.
15	- Rival enforcement is config-drift only: they check the rules arrived; nothing checks the rules are followed.
16	- The rule-sync category is nearly all free OSS under 3k stars; the one hosted SaaS (rulesync.dev) is in free beta.
17	- Skills won the content war: anthropics/skills hit 165k stars; SKILL.md is a ~40-tool cross-vendor standard.
18	- Enterprise scorecard vendors (Cortex, Port, OpsLevel) now sell AI-agent governance from above; OpsLevel's Tidra ships auto-PRs.
19	- The AGENTS.md spec stays minimal by design — no enforcement, versioning, or packaging — leaving that layer open.
20	
21	## The substrate: per-repo convention files
22	
23	Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
24	file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
25	with them:
26	
27	- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown,
28	  no-frontmatter file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August
29	  2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on
30	  December 9, 2025 — alongside MCP and Block's goose, with AWS, Anthropic,
31	  Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as platinum members — citing adoption by more
32	  than 60,000 open-source projects.
33	  *Correction (2026-07-31):* this page previously said "read by 30+ agents,"
34	  citing the codersera guide; that page actually says "native support in 20+
35	  tools," and the "30+" figure appears to have been conflated with Ruler's
36	  own supported-agent marketing. The scale citation is now the LF
37	  announcement (primary).
38	- The spec itself is deliberately minimal — "a README for agents," no
39	  required fields, no schema — and says nothing about enforcement, machine
40	  checks, versioning, or packaged conventions. The only shared semantics are
41	  precedence (nearest file wins; chat instructions override). Enforcement and
42	  packaging are out of scope, i.e. open territory.
43	- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's project-memory file, now a four-level
44	  hierarchy (managed policy / user / project / local) plus path-scoped
45	  `.claude/rules/` files and `@path` imports. Claude Code still reads
46	  CLAUDE.md natively, not AGENTS.md — the docs recommend an `@AGENTS.md`
47	  import or symlink as the bridge. Community best practice still converges on
48	  keeping it under ~200 lines (spot-checked 2026-07-31: the cited guide is
49	  alive and still says this).
50	- **SKILL.md / Agent Skills** became a cross-vendor open standard: Anthropic
51	  published the spec (agentskills.io, Dec 2025), and by mid-2026 roughly 40
52	  tools — OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, JetBrains
53	  Junie, Block's goose — read the same format. anthropics/skills sits at
54	  ~165.3k stars (verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31). The spec mandates only
55	  `name`/`description` frontmatter; nothing about checks or distribution.
56	- **Cursor** keeps its `.cursor/rules/` directory; Cursor Teams now also
57	  markets "Team Commands" with a team baseline and drift detection — the
58	  platform vendor absorbing single-tool rule sharing natively.
59	- **GitHub Copilot** keeps `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and reads
60	  AGENTS.md; GitHub's own blog mined 2,500+ AGENTS.md files for guidance.
61	
62	None of these substrate formats answer the question Claudinite is for: how
63	the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares it,
64	stays current there, and is *checked* rather than trusted.
65	
66	## The platform layer: what Claude Code now ships natively
67	
68	The largest competitive change since this page was seeded is Anthropic's own
69	distribution stack (all verified against current Claude Code docs,
70	2026-07-31):
71	
72	- **Plugins** (announced October 9, 2025) bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
73	  servers, LSP servers, and default settings into versioned packages,
74	  distributed through decentralized **marketplaces** (`marketplace.json` in
75	  any git repo/npm source, semver or SHA pinning, background auto-update).
76	- **Plugins can be centrally mandated**: project-level
77	  `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins`, managed-settings force-enable,
78	  `strictKnownMarketplaces` lockdown, container seed dirs, and claude.ai
79	  org-level plugin sync on Team/Enterprise plans.
80	- **Managed settings** give admins non-overridable org-wide permission rules,
81	  hooks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), MCP allowlists, model restrictions, and
82	  even an org-wide CLAUDE.md blob — delivered by MDM, machine-wide.
83	- **Hooks** provide deterministic in-session blocking (exit code 2 /
84	  `permissionDecision: "deny"`); Anthropic's own docs route enforcement away
85	  from prose to hooks — validating Claudinite's thesis while shipping the
86	  session-side half of it.
87	- **Native scheduling** arrived in three tiers (session cron//loop, cloud
88	  Routines, Desktop tasks); **auto memory** is per-project learnings that are
89	  explicitly machine-local and never shared.
90	
91	What the native stack still does **not** do — the whitespace Claudinite
92	occupies (absence verified across the plugins/marketplaces/settings/memory
93	docs): plugins converge *clients* (a per-user cache outside the repo), not
94	*repos*; nothing runs convention checks in CI; nothing opens PRs against
95	consuming repos to converge committed files with a canon; and no path exists
96	from one developer's local learnings to a reviewed shared canon. The risk to
97	watch is pace: scheduled tasks, auto memory, and org plugin sync all shipped
98	within about nine months.
99	
100	## Direct rivals: syncing rules across repos
101	
102	The category is crowded, young (almost everything created May 2025–June
103	2026), fragmented, and almost entirely free OSS. Star counts verified via
104	GitHub API on 2026-07-31:
105	
106	- **intellectronica/ruler** (2,833 ★, active) — "Centralise Your AI Coding
107	  Assistant Instructions"; a `.ruler/` directory concatenated into 30+
108	  agent-specific files. Single-repo only. Its README does ship a CI example
109	  that fails on uncommitted generated-file diffs — file-drift checking, the
110	  category's strongest "enforcement."
111	- **dyoshikawa/rulesync** (1,273 ★, 298 npm releases, very active) — CLI
112	  generating configs for 30+ tools from one `.rulesync/` source. Its
113	  supported-tools matrix now lists "checks" and "hooks" as feature columns —
114	  category vocabulary drifting toward checks without shipping enforcement.
115	- **RuleSync (rulesync.dev)** — the only commercial player found: a hosted
116	  dashboard + `rsc pull/push` CLI syncing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules
117	  across repos, with a CI-failable `check` command. Free during beta, team
118	  plans "planned." Ranks #1 for the literal query "sync CLAUDE.md across
119	  repos." Unrelated to the dyoshikawa CLI despite the name.

1	# Methods
2	
3	How the industry solved "propagate a convention across many repos and keep it
4	enforced" before AI coding agents existed. These are analogy and lesson
5	sources, not competitors: each system here picked a propagation model, an
6	enforcement model, and a drift story, and their fates predict what a
7	convention-pack product needs. Competitive landscape lives in
8	[`Market/`](../Market/README.md); pricing detail in
9	[`Business/`](../Business/README.md).
10	
11	## Key insights
12	
13	- The winning pattern is pin-in-repo plus a bot that opens update PRs — pre-commit and Renovate both ride it.
14	- pre-commit.ci monetizes exactly Claudinite's loop shape: free for OSS, $10–100/mo flat org tiers for private repos.
15	- Renovate's bot is free lead-gen; Mend charges (~$250/dev/yr) for scale, reporting and SLA — never for the mechanism.
16	- Peril — central org-wide rules, zero per-repo setup — died when GitHub Actions absorbed it; platform absorption kills.
17	- ESLint's flat-config break stranded eslint-config-airbnb: a pack format is an API; breaking it orphans the installed base.
18	- Bare template-sync (cruft, actions-template-sync) never broke 2k stars: the sync mechanism alone is not a product.
19	- GitHub itself gates org-wide enforcement behind paid plans — org rulesets were Enterprise-only until June 2025.
20	
21	## Two propagation archetypes
22	
23	Across nine systems studied, propagation splits cleanly:
24	
25	- **Pin-in-repo + bot-driven update PRs.** The consuming repo carries a small
26	  config with an exact version pin; a bot keeps the pin fresh via PRs.
27	  pre-commit (`rev:` pins + `autoupdate`, and pre-commit.ci's weekly
28	  autoupdate PRs), cruft/copier (recorded template pin + scheduled update
29	  PRs), ESLint shareable configs (semver pin in the lockfile + Renovate
30	  bumps). This archetype dominates *file-based* convention distribution.
31	- **Dynamic central resolution, no per-repo pin.** Renovate `extends` presets
32	  re-resolve from the preset repo's default branch on every run; OPA agents
33	  poll signed bundles from a control plane; Allstar and GitHub org rulesets
34	  enforce server-side. Pin-less live resolution is chosen only where the
35	  operator also owns the runtime and cannot break the consumer's own CI.
36	
37	Claudinite's baselining (vendored corpus converged nightly to canon head via
38	auto-PRs) is structurally the first archetype's *mechanism* with the second
39	archetype's *no-pin policy* — a combination none of the winners chose; see
40	[`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md) for the gap this opens.
41	
42	## What the winners did
43	
44	- **pre-commit** (~15.5k ★): a single small config file in the consuming
45	  repo, exact `rev` pins so repos never silently change behavior, and an
46	  explicit `autoupdate` command. Enforcement is local hooks plus
47	  `pre-commit run --all-files` in CI.
48	- **pre-commit.ci** monetizes the loop as a hosted bot: zero-configuration
49	  setup beyond the existing config file, auto-fixing PRs (it pushes fix
50	  commits onto the PR branch), and automated weekly pin updates. Free for
51	  open source; $10/mo personal private, $20/mo orgs ≤25 users, $100/mo orgs
52	  ≤100 users — flat org tiers, identical features across tiers.
53	- **Renovate**: the hosted GitHub App is free with 71,414 marketplace
54	  installs; org-wide adoption is one onboarding PR (it auto-detects an
55	  org-level `renovate-config` repo). Its enforcement is auto-PRs only — it
56	  never gates CI itself. Mend monetizes Enterprise Edition (~$250 per
57	  contributing developer/year, third-party figure) on scale, Merge
58	  Confidence, reporting APIs, and SLA — the mechanism stays free.
59	- **ESLint shareable configs**: registry+semver+lockfile propagation at
60	  enormous scale (eslint-config-prettier ~61M weekly downloads). Nobody
61	  monetized the distribution itself; value accrued to adjacent services.
62	
63	Four traits recur across the winners: a single small file in the consuming
64	repo; near-zero-effort adoption (zero-config or an auto-generated onboarding
65	PR); drift handled by bots opening PRs, not by humans; CI-fail enforcement
66	softened by autofix.
67	
68	## Cautionary tales
69	
70	- **Peril** (hosted Danger: centrally-stored org-wide Dangerfiles, zero
71	  per-repo setup — the closest structural ancestor to a convention canon)
72	  went to maintenance mode after its creator concluded "80% of Peril is
73	  available today in GitHub Actions." Central-rules products die when the
74	  platform absorbs their mechanism.
75	- **GitHub required workflows** were killed and folded into repository
76	  rulesets within roughly a year (GA October 2023) — platform-native
77	  enforcement primitives churn, which cuts both ways for anyone building on
78	  them.
79	- **The ESLint flat-config migration** stranded the ecosystem's flagship
80	  convention package: eslint-config-airbnb never shipped flat-config support
81	  and its TypeScript companion was archived May 2025, handing the installed
82	  base to forks and shims. A pack format is an API; a breaking format change
83	  can orphan every consumer.
84	- **Copy-based template sync stayed niche**: cruft (~1.6k ★) ships `cruft
85	  check` for CI drift detection and a README recipe for a weekly
86	  drift-PR workflow — literally Claudinite's baselining loop as a DIY recipe
87	  since ~2020 — and actions-template-sync (~327 ★) does scheduled
88	  merge-upstream PRs. Neither broke out. The sync mechanism alone, without
89	  curated content and enforcement, is not a product.
90	- **copier** has the most sophisticated drift-merge algorithm in the family
91	  (regenerate old template, diff to extract local changes, re-apply over the
92	  new template, inline conflict markers) — sophistication that still didn't
93	  buy adoption (~3.5k ★).
94	
95	## Enforcement-model spectrum
96	
97	- **Advisory graduated**: Danger's fail/warn/message levels (~5.5k ★, never
98	  commercialized) — the graduated blocking-vs-advisory distinction is the
99	  design export, matching Claudinite's blocking/advisory severities.
100	- **Settings-not-content**: OpenSSF Allstar (org-wide GitHub policy app,
101	  log → auto-issue → auto-fix ladder) and GitHub org rulesets enforce
102	  *platform settings and required checks*, never file content inside repos.
103	  Org rulesets were Enterprise-only until June 16, 2025 (then extended to
104	  Team plans) — GitHub prices org-wide enforcement as a premium.
105	- **Fallback-without-copying**: GitHub's default community health files
106	  (org-level `.github` repo applies wherever a repo lacks its own copy) —
107	  zero drift by construction but limited to a fixed whitelist of file types.
108	- **Runtime pull**: OPA distributes signed, versioned policy bundles agents
109	  poll and activate atomically — a control-plane convergence loop
110	  structurally identical to canon→repos, at runtime instead of via git.
111	  conftest pushes/pulls the same bundles through OCI registries — an
112	  emerging "policy packs as OCI artifacts" distribution norm.
113	- **URL-inheritance + autofix**: MegaLinter's remote `EXTENDS` config merge
114	  plus APPLY_FIXES delivered as commit or PR.
115	
116	## Lessons for a convention-pack product
117	
118	Read directly off the corpus: pinned versions with bot-opened update PRs as
119	the drift mechanism (not silent head-tracking); one-command or zero-config
120	adoption; CI-fail enforcement paired with autofix to keep friction low;
121	free-for-OSS plus flat private tiers or per-dev enterprise pricing; treat the
122	pack format as a stable API; and expect the platform (GitHub, Anthropic) to
123	absorb any mechanism that isn't paired with curated, maintained content.

44	- A **growth loop implemented end-to-end repo-side**: conversation capture

53	1. **Enforcement depth.** Checks that block the agent's session *and* gate
54	   CI, with what/why/fix findings and reason-required acceptances. Matching

56	   model — not a sync script. No rival ships any of it (Market wiki).

64	   memory) is explicitly machine-local and never shared; no rival has any
65	   analog (Market wiki).

## Organization-Level Plugin Management

On Team or Enterprise plans, an owner can distribute plugins across your organization through plugin marketplaces. Admins can set per-plugin installation preferences to control which plugins are auto-installed, available for self-service, or hidden from your organization's catalog.

## Plugin Installation Preferences

Each plugin in your marketplace has an organization-wide installation preference (Installed by default, Available for install, Required, or Not available). Auto-installed plugins appear in their installed list automatically.

## Enterprise-Specific Features

On Enterprise plans, admins can also override these preferences for specific groups—for example, auto-installing a plugin for one team while hiding it from everyone else. On Enterprise plans, your admin may customize which plugins are available to your group.

## Auto-Install Configuration

A repository's .claude/settings.json can specify an extraKnownMarketplaces entry pointing to your company's plugin marketplace, and you can list certain plugins under enabledPlugins in the settings to have them auto-enabled by default for the project. However, plugins configured in org managed settings (extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins) do not auto-install in the CLI.

## Agent Conventions & Standardization (2026)

AGENTS.md is converging as a cross-tool standard, addressing the fragmentation problem where one agent reads AGENTS.md, another expects CLAUDE.md, GitHub Copilot wants .github/copilot-instructions.md, and Gemini CLI looks for .gemini/GEMINI.md.

## Agent-Kit: Auto-Derivation Tool

There is an emerging solution to this convergence problem: agent-kit derives CLAUDE.md, .gemini/GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and CONVENTIONS.md from a single AGENTS.md. @mongez/agent-kit is a small CLI + TypeScript library that derives every per-agent instructions file from a single AGENTS.md.

This approach addresses the core problem that teams maintaining multiple agents end up with several near-identical copies of the same instructions, and when someone edits one and not the others, they drift apart.

The broader goal is to maintain one instruction file (AGENTS.md) and add CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules only when you need features specific to those tools.

# Claude Code CLI Plugin Auto-Install Issue

**Issue Title:** CLI: Auto-install plugins from org managed settings (extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins) #45323

**State:** Closed as not planned

**Creation Date:** April 8, 2026

## Issue Summary

The issue reports that plugins configured in organization managed settings (`extraKnownMarketplaces` + `enabledPlugins`) do **not auto-install in the CLI**, despite working correctly in the desktop and web apps.

### Current Behavior
1. Admin configures `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins` in managed settings
2. CLI fetches managed settings at startup → cached in `~/.claude/remote-settings.json`
3. **The marketplace is NOT automatically registered** in `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json`
4. **The plugin is NOT automatically installed**
5. Users must manually run `/plugin marketplace add` and `/plugin install`

### Expected Behavior
Plugins listed in `enabledPlugins` should automatically install when the CLI starts, eliminating the need for manual installation steps.

## Workarounds Attempted
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`: Requires baking plugins into Docker images at build time
- Entrypoint scripts: Add startup latency and require runtime network/auth
- Manual installation docs: Defeats the purpose of org-managed settings

**Confirming Details:** The issue was marked as closed "not planned," indicating this feature request was not implemented in the CLI despite being filed multiple times as related feature requests (#23737, #28310).

content.content:
1	# Market
2	
3	The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
4	coding-agent user already has on disk, the platform-native layer Anthropic now
5	ships itself, the direct rule-sync competitors, the adjacent content
6	ecosystems, and the enterprise vendors encroaching from above. Business models
7	and price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); customer
8	segments in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md); what this means for
9	Claudinite in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).
10	
11	## Key insights
12	
13	- Anthropic ships the session half natively, but CLI auto-install of org-mandated plugins was closed "not planned."
14	- Nobody — native or rival — converges repos: no auto-PR loop from a canon, no CI convention gates, no shared growth loop.
15	- Rival enforcement is config-drift only: they check the rules arrived; nothing checks the rules are followed.
16	- The rule-sync category is nearly all free OSS under 3k stars; the one hosted SaaS (rulesync.dev) is in free beta.
17	- Skills won the content war: anthropics/skills hit 165k stars; SKILL.md is a ~40-tool cross-vendor standard.
18	- Enterprise scorecard vendors (Cortex, Port, OpsLevel) now sell AI-agent governance from above; OpsLevel's Tidra ships auto-PRs.
19	- The AGENTS.md spec stays minimal by design — no enforcement, versioning, or packaging — leaving that layer open.
20	
21	## The substrate: per-repo convention files
22	
23	Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
24	file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
25	with them:
26	
27	- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown,
28	  no-frontmatter file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August
29	  2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on
30	  December 9, 2025 — alongside MCP and Block's goose, with AWS, Anthropic,
31	  Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as platinum members — citing adoption by more
32	  than 60,000 open-source projects.
33	  *Correction (2026-07-31):* this page previously said "read by 30+ agents,"
34	  citing the codersera guide; that page actually says "native support in 20+
35	  tools," and the "30+" figure appears to have been conflated with Ruler's
36	  own supported-agent marketing. The scale citation is now the LF
37	  announcement (primary).
38	- The spec itself is deliberately minimal — "a README for agents," no
39	  required fields, no schema — and says nothing about enforcement, machine
40	  checks, versioning, or packaged conventions. The only shared semantics are
41	  precedence (nearest file wins; chat instructions override). Enforcement and
42	  packaging are out of scope, i.e. open territory.
43	- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's project-memory file, now a four-level
44	  hierarchy (managed policy / user / project / local) plus path-scoped
45	  `.claude/rules/` files and `@path` imports. Claude Code still reads
46	  CLAUDE.md natively, not AGENTS.md — the docs recommend an `@AGENTS.md`
47	  import or symlink as the bridge. Community best practice still converges on
48	  keeping it under ~200 lines (spot-checked 2026-07-31: the cited guide is
49	  alive and still says this).
50	- **SKILL.md / Agent Skills** became a cross-vendor open standard: Anthropic
51	  published the spec (agentskills.io, Dec 2025), and by mid-2026 roughly 40
52	  tools — OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, JetBrains
53	  Junie, Block's goose — read the same format. anthropics/skills sits at
54	  ~165.3k stars (verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31). The spec mandates only
55	  `name`/`description` frontmatter; nothing about checks or distribution.
56	- **Cursor** keeps its `.cursor/rules/` directory; Cursor Teams now also
57	  markets "Team Commands" with a team baseline and drift detection — the
58	  platform vendor absorbing single-tool rule sharing natively.
59	- **GitHub Copilot** keeps `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and reads
60	  AGENTS.md; GitHub's own blog mined 2,500+ AGENTS.md files for guidance.
61	
62	None of these substrate formats answer the question Claudinite is for: how
63	the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares it,
64	stays current there, and is *checked* rather than trusted.
65	
66	## The platform layer: what Claude Code now ships natively
67	
68	The largest competitive change since this page was seeded is Anthropic's own
69	distribution stack (all verified against current Claude Code docs,
70	2026-07-31):
71	
72	- **Plugins** (announced October 9, 2025) bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
73	  servers, LSP servers, and default settings into versioned packages,
74	  distributed through decentralized **marketplaces** (`marketplace.json` in
75	  any git repo/npm source, semver or SHA pinning, background auto-update).
76	- **Plugins can be centrally mandated — but not uniformly across surfaces.**
77	  Project-level `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins`, managed-settings
78	  force-enable, `strictKnownMarketplaces` lockdown, container seed dirs, and
79	  claude.ai org-level plugin sync on Team/Enterprise plans (per-plugin
80	  installation preferences — Installed by default / Available for install /
81	  Required / Not available) all exist as mechanisms.
82	  *Correction (2026-08-09):* this page previously left the impression the
83	  CLI itself honors `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` automatically.
84	  It doesn't. [anthropics/claude-code#45323](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45323)
85	  ("CLI: Auto-install plugins from org managed settings") documents that the
86	  CLI fetches the managed-settings marketplace into
87	  `~/.claude/remote-settings.json` at startup but never registers it in
88	  `known_marketplaces.json` or installs the listed plugin — the org's admin
89	  still has to have every user run `/plugin marketplace add` and
90	  `/plugin install` by hand, or bake plugins into a container image at build
91	  time via `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`. Filed April 2026, the issue was
92	  closed **"not planned."** The same managed settings *do* auto-install on
93	  the desktop and web apps per the issue's own comparison and the Claude
94	  Help Center's org-plugin-management article (that page egress-blocked to
95	  this pass's fetcher — via search-quoted context, not opened directly) — so
96	  the CLI, Claudinite's own delivery surface, is specifically the one where
97	  central mandate still isn't unattended.
98	- **Managed settings** give admins non-overridable org-wide permission rules,
99	  hooks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), MCP allowlists, model restrictions, and
100	  even an org-wide CLAUDE.md blob — delivered by MDM, machine-wide.
101	- **Hooks** provide deterministic in-session blocking (exit code 2 /
102	  `permissionDecision: "deny"`); Anthropic's own docs route enforcement away
103	  from prose to hooks — validating Claudinite's thesis while shipping the
104	  session-side half of it.
105	- **Native scheduling** arrived in three tiers (session cron//loop, cloud
106	  Routines, Desktop tasks); **auto memory** is per-project learnings that are
107	  explicitly machine-local and never shared.
108	
109	What the native stack still does **not** do — the whitespace Claudinite
110	occupies (absence verified across the plugins/marketplaces/settings/memory
111	docs): plugins converge *clients* (a per-user cache outside the repo), not
112	*repos*; nothing runs convention checks in CI; nothing opens PRs against
113	consuming repos to converge committed files with a canon; and no path exists
114	from one developer's local learnings to a reviewed shared canon. Even the
115	client-convergence story is uneven today: centrally-mandated plugins land
116	unattended on the desktop/web apps but not in the CLI, where the same
117	managed-settings config still needs a human running install commands (or a
118	container image baked ahead of time) — Anthropic's own tracker calls this
119	"not planned," not merely unshipped. The risk to watch is pace: scheduled
120	tasks, auto memory, and org plugin sync all shipped within about nine
121	months.
122	
123	## Direct rivals: syncing rules across repos
124	
125	The category is crowded, young (almost everything created May 2025–June
126	2026), fragmented, and almost entirely free OSS. Star counts verified via
127	GitHub API on 2026-07-31:
128	
129	- **intellectronica/ruler** (2,833 ★, active) — "Centralise Your AI Coding
130	  Assistant Instructions"; a `.ruler/` directory concatenated into 30+
131	  agent-specific files. Single-repo only. Its README does ship a CI example
132	  that fails on uncommitted generated-file diffs — file-drift checking, the
133	  category's strongest "enforcement."
134	- **dyoshikawa/rulesync** (1,273 ★, 298 npm releases, very active) — CLI
135	  generating configs for 30+ tools from one `.rulesync/` source. Its
136	  supported-tools matrix now lists "checks" and "hooks" as feature columns —
137	  category vocabulary drifting toward checks without shipping enforcement.
138	- **RuleSync (rulesync.dev)** — the only commercial player found: a hosted
139	  dashboard + `rsc pull/push` CLI syncing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules
140	  across repos, with a CI-failable `check` command. Free during beta, team
141	  plans "planned." Ranks #1 for the literal query "sync CLAUDE.md across
142	  repos." Unrelated to the dyoshikawa CLI despite the name.
143	- **Goldziher/ai-rulez** (135 ★) — the rival with the strongest enforcement
144	  language: pre-commit hooks literally named `ai-rulez-enforce`, a
145	  `verify` command, and cross-repo "remote includes." All of it targets
146	  config-file integrity, not the code the agent writes.
147	- **agent-sh/agnix** (372 ★, Rust) — a 444-rule *linter for agent config
148	  files* (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hooks, MCP) with a CI GitHub
149	  Action. No sync; complementary evidence for the checks-on-config trend.
150	- **yujiosaka/knowhub** (41 ★) — dormant: last push 2025-07-24, two npm
151	  releases ever. The earlier open question about its enforcement is answered:
152	  file-sync verification only.
153	- **lbb00/ai-rules-sync** (35 ★) — cross-repo team sharing via symlinked
154	  central git repos, 12+ tools; npm activity stalled March 2026. No
155	  enforcement.
156	- **fabian-barney/ai-rules** (3 ★) — a content repo vendored via git subtree
157	  pinned to tagged releases; prior art for the vendored-versioned-unit idea,
158	  no tooling.
159	- **Sync AI Agent Rules** (GitHub Action, 1 ★) — compiles layered rules from
160	  a central repo and auto-commits them into agent files; pushes updates,
161	  gates nothing.
162	- **ranyitz/aicm** (36 ★) — closest architectural precedent to packs:
163	  installable npm packages bundling rules/commands/skills/hooks
164	  (`@company/ai-preset`), but outputs are regenerated into gitignored dirs,
165	  and no enforcement or convergence.
166	- Fragmentation is extreme: at least ten distinct repos named "agentsync"
167	  were created Dec 2025–Jun 2026, all under 60 stars — nobody owns the niche.
168	
169	Category-level answers to this page's former open questions:
170	
171	- **Enforcement**: yes-but-narrowly. Five tools advertise CI-failable checks
172	  (ruler, ai-rulez, agnix, rulesync.dev, spxrogers/agentsync), every one
173	  scoped to config-file drift or config-file lint. None runs checks on the
174	  work product, blocks an agent session, or opens convergence PRs. The
175	  sharpened differentiation line: *they check that the rules arrived;
176	  Claudinite checks that the rules are followed.*
177	- **Business models**: except hosted RuleSync, every surveyed tool (15+) is
178	  unmonetized MIT/Apache/Unlicense OSS — an opening, and a price-anchor risk.
179	- **Marketing**: every headline is a movement verb (synchronize / centralise /
180	  share / find); multi-agent breadth (30+/31/20/12+ tools) is the default
181	  marketing axis, making Claudinite's Claude-Code-only focus unusual in the
182	  field. No rival names enforcement in its headline.
183	
184	## Adjacent gravity wells
185	
186	- **Vercel's `npx skills` ecosystem** — vercel-labs/skills (27,660 ★) and
187	  vercel-labs/agent-skills (29,638 ★) in about six months: a "package manager
188	  for AI coding agents" across 17+ agents, with the skills.sh directory.
189	  Distribution only — no checks, no CI, no convergence — but it validates
190	  versioned vendored agent-knowledge packages at two orders of magnitude more
191	  adoption than any rule-sync tool.
192	- **Curated content lists**: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (51,368 ★)
193	  overtook the 8-months-older PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules (40,476 ★) —
194	  convention-sharing energy has moved to Claude Code. Fork counts (3.4k/4.4k)
195	  indicate copy-into-my-project behavior with no update path.
196	- **steipete/agent-rules** (5,702 ★), the category's most-starred rules
197	  content repo, is archived — static rules-content repos are being
198	  superseded, plausibly by the skills ecosystem.
199	- **cursor.directory** monetizes free rules browsing indirectly (~$35k/mo via
200	  jobs/ads per its founder's public claims) — attention, not governance.
201	- **davila7/claude-code-templates** (30,020 ★, aitmpl.com) is the largest
202	  community hub for Claude Code assets, independent of Anthropic's plugin
203	  system.
204	
205	## From above: enterprise scorecard vendors
206	
207	Internal-developer-portal vendors sell "standards enforced across many
208	repos" to enterprises as **scorecards** (checks graded across a service
209	fleet, with levels and campaign deadlines), and in 2025–2026 every one of
210	them pivoted to AI-agent governance:
211	
212	- **Cortex** rebranded "mission control for the AI software factory" and
213	  ships AI-governance scorecards that check "which repositories have proper
214	  AI instructions" — observation of config presence, not authoring or
215	  convergence. It published Claudinite's exact thesis as marketing: "AI is
216	  writing your code. Who's watching your standards?" (Sept 2025).
217	- **Port** repositioned as an "Agentic SDLC" platform that auto-discovers
218	  "agents, MCPs, skills so you can enforce your standards."
219	- **OpsLevel** markets a portal that "enforces standards automatically" and
220	  spun out **Tidra AI** — the one IDP product found that *remediates* with
221	  auto-PRs across every repo in scope (campaign-driven, not a continuous
222	  convergence-to-canon loop).
223	- **Spotify Soundcheck** (paid Backstage plugin) shipped MCP actions so
224	  Claude Code and Cursor can *query* failing checks — scorecards made
225	  readable by agents, the inverse of governing what agents follow.
226	- The category norm remains observe-and-nudge (notifications, Jira tickets,
227	  deadlines); default-on auto-PR convergence stays ahead of it.
228	
229	Deeper enterprise-buyer analysis (procurement gates, ranked requirements)
230	lives in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md).
231

314	  managed settings") — filed April 2026, closed **"not planned"** — which
315	  shows the CLI never auto-installs `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces`

[Resource from github at repo://[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/sha/f66d779830d4287cd911d72d103ec14d12406909/contents/product-wiki/Market/README.md] # Market

The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
coding-agent user already has on disk, the platform-native layer Anthropic now
ships itself, the direct rule-sync competitors, the adjacent content
ecosystems, and the enterprise vendors encroaching from above. Business models
and price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); customer
segments in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md); what this means for
Claudinite in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).

## Key insights

- Anthropic now ships the session half natively: plugins bundle skills+hooks+MCP and can be force-enabled org-wide.
- Nobody — native or rival — converges repos: no auto-PR loop from a canon, no CI convention gates, no shared growth loop.
- Rival enforcement is config-drift only: they check the rules arrived; nothing checks the rules are followed.
- The rule-sync category is nearly all free OSS under 3k stars; the one hosted SaaS (rulesync.dev) is in free beta.
- Skills won the content war: anthropics/skills hit 165k stars; SKILL.md is a ~40-tool cross-vendor standard.
- Enterprise scorecard vendors (Cortex, Port, OpsLevel) now sell AI-agent governance from above; OpsLevel's Tidra ships auto-PRs.
- The AGENTS.md spec stays minimal by design — no enforcement, versioning, or packaging — leaving that layer open.

## The substrate: per-repo convention files

Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
with them:

- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown,
  no-frontmatter file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August
  2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on
  December 9, 2025 — alongside MCP and Block's goose, with AWS, Anthropic,
  Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as platinum members — citing adoption by more
  than 60,000 open-source projects.
  *Correction (2026-07-31):* this page previously said "read by 30+ agents,"
  citing the codersera guide; that page actually says "native support in 20+
  tools," and the "30+" figure appears to have been conflated with Ruler's
  own supported-agent marketing. The scale citation is now the LF
  announcement (primary).
- The spec itself is deliberately minimal — "a README for agents," no
  required fields, no schema — and says nothing about enforcement, machine
  checks, versioning, or packaged conventions. The only shared semantics are
  precedence (nearest file wins; chat instructions override). Enforcement and
  packaging are out of scope, i.e. open territory.
- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's project-memory file, now a four-level
  hierarchy (managed policy / user / project / local) plus path-scoped
  `.claude/rules/` files and `@path` imports. Claude Code still reads
  CLAUDE.md natively, not AGENTS.md — the docs recommend an `@AGENTS.md`
  import or symlink as the bridge. Community best practice still converges on
  keeping it under ~200 lines (spot-checked 2026-07-31: the cited guide is
  alive and still says this).
- **SKILL.md / Agent Skills** became a cross-vendor open standard: Anthropic
  published the spec (agentskills.io, Dec 2025), and by mid-2026 roughly 40
  tools — OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, JetBrains
  Junie, Block's goose — read the same format. anthropics/skills sits at
  ~165.3k stars (verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31). The spec mandates only
  `name`/`description` frontmatter; nothing about checks or distribution.
- **Cursor** keeps its `.cursor/rules/` directory; Cursor Teams now also
  markets "Team Commands" with a team baseline and drift detection — the
  platform vendor absorbing single-tool rule sharing natively.
- **GitHub Copilot** keeps `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and reads
  AGENTS.md; GitHub's own blog mined 2,500+ AGENTS.md files for guidance.

None of these substrate formats answer the question Claudinite is for: how
the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares it,
stays current there, and is *checked* rather than trusted.

## The platform layer: what Claude Code now ships natively

The largest competitive change since this page was seeded is Anthropic's own
distribution stack (all verified against current Claude Code docs,
2026-07-31):

- **Plugins** (announced October 9, 2025) bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
  servers, LSP servers, and default settings into versioned packages,
  distributed through decentralized **marketplaces** (`marketplace.json` in
  any git repo/npm source, semver or SHA pinning, background auto-update).
- **Plugins can be centrally mandated**: project-level
  `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins`, managed-settings force-enable,
  `strictKnownMarketplaces` lockdown, container seed dirs, and claude.ai
  org-level plugin sync on Team/Enterprise plans.
- **Managed settings** give admins non-overridable org-wide permission rules,
  hooks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), MCP allowlists, model restrictions, and
  even an org-wide CLAUDE.md blob — delivered by MDM, machine-wide.
- **Hooks** provide deterministic in-session blocking (exit code 2 /
  `permissionDecision: "deny"`); Anthropic's own docs route enforcement away
  from prose to hooks — validating Claudinite's thesis while shipping the
  session-side half of it.
- **Native scheduling** arrived in three tiers (session cron//loop, cloud
  Routines, Desktop tasks); **auto memory** is per-project learnings that are
  explicitly machine-local and never shared.

What the native stack still does **not** do — the whitespace Claudinite
occupies (absence verified across the plugins/marketplaces/settings/memory
docs): plugins converge *clients* (a per-user cache outside the repo), not
*repos*; nothing runs convention checks in CI; nothing opens PRs against
consuming repos to converge committed files with a canon; and no path exists
from one developer's local learnings to a reviewed shared canon. The risk to
watch is pace: scheduled tasks, auto memory, and org plugin sync all shipped
within about nine months.

## Direct rivals: syncing rules across repos

The category is crowded, young (almost everything created May 2025–June
2026), fragmented, and almost entirely free OSS. Star counts verified via
GitHub API on 2026-07-31:

- **intellectronica/ruler** (2,833 ★, active) — "Centralise Your AI Coding
  Assistant Instructions"; a `.ruler/` directory concatenated into 30+
  agent-specific files. Single-repo only. Its README does ship a CI example
  that fails on uncommitted generated-file diffs — file-drift checking, the
  category's strongest "enforcement."
- **dyoshikawa/rulesync** (1,273 ★, 298 npm releases, very active) — CLI
  generating configs for 30+ tools from one `.rulesync/` source. Its
  supported-tools matrix now lists "checks" and "hooks" as feature columns —
  category vocabulary drifting toward checks without shipping enforcement.
- **RuleSync (rulesync.dev)** — the only commercial player found: a hosted
  dashboard + `rsc pull/push` CLI syncing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules
  across repos, with a CI-failable `check` command. Free during beta, team
  plans "planned." Ranks #1 for the literal query "sync CLAUDE.md across
  repos." Unrelated to the dyoshikawa CLI despite the name.
- **Goldziher/ai-rulez** (135 ★) — the rival with the strongest enforcement
  language: pre-commit hooks literally named `ai-rulez-enforce`, a
  `verify` command, and cross-repo "remote includes." All of it targets
  config-file integrity, not the code the agent writes.
- **agent-sh/agnix** (372 ★, Rust) — a 444-rule *linter for agent config
  files* (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hooks, MCP) with a CI GitHub
  Action. No sync; complementary evidence for the checks-on-config trend.
- **yujiosaka/knowhub** (41 ★) — dormant: last push 2025-07-24, two npm
  releases ever. The earlier open question about its enforcement is answered:
  file-sync verification only.
- **lbb00/ai-rules-sync** (35 ★) — cross-repo team sharing via symlinked
  central git repos, 12+ tools; npm activity stalled March 2026. No
  enforcement.
- **fabian-barney/ai-rules** (3 ★) — a content repo vendored via git subtree
  pinned to tagged releases; prior art for the vendored-versioned-unit idea,
  no tooling.
- **Sync AI Agent Rules** (GitHub Action, 1 ★) — compiles layered rules from
  a central repo and auto-commits them into agent files; pushes updates,
  gates nothing.
- **ranyitz/aicm** (36 ★) — closest architectural precedent to packs:
  installable npm packages bundling rules/commands/skills/hooks
  (`@company/ai-preset`), but outputs are regenerated into gitignored dirs,
  and no enforcement or convergence.
- Fragmentation is extreme: at least ten distinct repos named "agentsync"
  were created Dec 2025–Jun 2026, all under 60 stars — nobody owns the niche.

Category-level answers to this page's former open questions:

- **Enforcement**: yes-but-narrowly. Five tools advertise CI-failable checks
  (ruler, ai-rulez, agnix, rulesync.dev, spxrogers/agentsync), every one
  scoped to config-file drift or config-file lint. None runs checks on the
  work product, blocks an agent session, or opens convergence PRs. The
  sharpened differentiation line: *they check that the rules arrived;
  Claudinite checks that the rules are followed.*
- **Business models**: except hosted RuleSync, every surveyed tool (15+) is
  unmonetized MIT/Apache/Unlicense OSS — an opening, and a price-anchor risk.
- **Marketing**: every headline is a movement verb (synchronize / centralise /
  share / find); multi-agent breadth (30+/31/20/12+ tools) is the default
  marketing axis, making Claudinite's Claude-Code-only focus unusual in the
  field. No rival names enforcement in its headline.

## Adjacent gravity wells

- **Vercel's `npx skills` ecosystem** — vercel-labs/skills (27,660 ★) and
  vercel-labs/agent-skills (29,638 ★) in about six months: a "package manager
  for AI coding agents" across 17+ agents, with the skills.sh directory.
  Distribution only — no checks, no CI, no convergence — but it validates
  versioned vendored agent-knowledge packages at two orders of magnitude more
  adoption than any rule-sync tool.
- **Curated content lists**: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (51,368 ★)
  overtook the 8-months-older PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules (40,476 ★) —
  convention-sharing energy has moved to Claude Code. Fork counts (3.4k/4.4k)
  indicate copy-into-my-project behavior with no update path.
- **steipete/agent-rules** (5,702 ★), the category's most-starred rules
  content repo, is archived — static rules-content repos are being
  superseded, plausibly by the skills ecosystem.
- **cursor.directory** monetizes free rules browsing indirectly (~$35k/mo via
  jobs/ads per its founder's public claims) — attention, not governance.
- **davila7/claude-code-templates** (30,020 ★, aitmpl.com) is the largest
  community hub for Claude Code assets, independent of Anthropic's plugin
  system.

## From above: enterprise scorecard vendors

Internal-developer-portal vendors sell "standards enforced across many
repos" to enterprises as **scorecards** (checks graded across a service
fleet, with levels and campaign deadlines), and in 2025–2026 every one of
them pivoted to AI-agent governance:

- **Cortex** rebranded "mission control for the AI software factory" and
  ships AI-governance scorecards that check "which repositories have proper
  AI instructions" — observation of config presence, not authoring or
  convergence. It published Claudinite's exact thesis as marketing: "AI is
  writing your code. Who's watching your standards?" (Sept 2025).
- **Port** repositioned as an "Agentic SDLC" platform that auto-discovers
  "agents, MCPs, skills so you can enforce your standards."
- **OpsLevel** markets a portal that "enforces standards automatically" and
  spun out **Tidra AI** — the one IDP product found that *remediates* with
  auto-PRs across every repo in scope (campaign-driven, not a continuous
  convergence-to-canon loop).
- **Spotify Soundcheck** (paid Backstage plugin) shipped MCP actions so
  Claude Code and Cursor can *query* failing checks — scorecards made
  readable by agents, the inverse of governing what agents follow.
- The category norm remains observe-and-nudge (notifications, Jira tickets,
  deadlines); default-on auto-PR convergence stays ahead of it.

Deeper enterprise-buyer analysis (procurement gates, ranked requirements)
lives in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md).
